data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A Fibonacci lattice (sunflower spiral) of 13 points scaled into the unit square is used for its quasi-random distribution, targeting a minimum triangle area of 0.006 to account for potential small triangles.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The Fibonacci spiral may naturally produce triangles with area smaller than 0.006.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checker might find a smaller triangle if the spiral points are too close in certain regions of the square.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The golden ratio spiral distributes 13 points in the unit square using (x, y) = ((k * alpha mod 1) * 0.96 + 0.02, (k * beta mod 1) * 0.96 + 0.02) where alpha = 1/phi \u2248 0.6180339887, beta = 1/phi^2 \u2248 0.3819660113, and k = 0..12. This distribution is known for low discrepancy, but it can have small triangles. A claim of 0.006 is set as a floor because the exact minimum area is uncertain and likely smaller than structured grids due to the quasi-random nature of the Fibonacci spiral.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
